solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Protective cover on sides of settee when painting

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece placed on another follows it
the sides of the word settee are its first and last letters

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a cape is a cloak worn as protective cover

explanation.surface: A decorator throws a dust sheet over the sofa's arms before painting the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'painting' looks like house decorating, but it is the definition: a picture of the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A seascape is a painting whose subject is the sea or coast.

clue.text: Traps ahead buried in batches

indicators.note: one word buried in another sits inside it

parts.note: sets are batches or groups
up means ahead, as a team two goals up

explanation.surface: Snares placed in front lie hidden among groups of things.
explanation.definitionFit: A setup is a trap or a scheme contrived to catch someone out.

clue.text: In modern times, life is thrown away

indicators.note: the scrambled word goes in the abbreviation for the modern era

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the modern era of dates

indicators.note: thrown means jumbled, so the word life is rearranged

explanation.surface: Nowadays people's lives get wasted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thrown away' looks like one phrase, but 'is thrown' is the anagram signal and 'away' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Afield means away from home, as in travelling far afield.

clue.text: Monsieur invested in exotic cargo, Frenchman's no primitive

indicators.note: to be invested in is to be put inside, so the letter goes within
exotic suggests something strange, so the letters of cargo are rearranged

parts.note: non is the French word for no

explanation.surface: A French trader puts his money into foreign freight and insists he is no backward man.
explanation.definitionFit: Cro-Magnon people were early modern humans of the Stone Age, a byword for primitive man.

clue.text: A dance in textbook popular with a lead dancer

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the word for a schoolbook

parts.note: a primer is an elementary textbook
a ball is a formal dance
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A schoolbook about dancing goes down well with a principal performer.
explanation.definitionFit: A prima ballerina is the leading female dancer of a ballet company.

clue.text: Running ahead, look around

parts.note: up means ahead, as in leading

indicators.note: turned around, the word for a quick look is read backwards

parts.note: a peek is a quick look

explanation.surface: A jogger at the front glances behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' looks like jogging, but it means the running of something: its maintenance.
explanation.definitionFit: Upkeep is the maintenance or running of a house, car or organisation, and its cost.

clue.text: Wine glass containing nothing

indicators.note: one word holds the other within it

parts.note: a pint is a glass of beer
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A wine glass sits empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinot is a family of grape varieties and the wine made from them, such as Pinot Noir.

clue.text: Eastern spies do overcome incidents

indicators.note: overcome suggests being upset or overturned, so the letters of spies do are rearranged

explanation.surface: Oriental agents triumph in various events.
explanation.definitionFit: Episodes are individual events or incidents in a sequence.

clue.text: Greek character capturing monarch spots jewels

indicators.note: the letter of the Greek alphabet captures, so holds, the royal letters

parts.note: pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for a monarch
dots are small spots

explanation.surface: A Greek figure seizing a king spies some gems.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridots are green gemstones, a variety of olivine used in jewellery.

clue.text: Liquid chocolate drunk all the time

indicators.note: liquid suggests something melted and flowing, so the letters of chocolate drunk are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sips hot chocolate constantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like the anagram signal, but it is part of the fodder; 'Liquid' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Round-the-clock means continuously, day and night, without stopping.

clue.text: Oil wasted on voyage to get to port city

indicators.note: in an across clue the scrambled piece is placed on, so after, the journey

parts.note: a trip is a journey or voyage

indicators.note: wasted suggests ruined, so the letters of oil are rearranged

explanation.surface: Fuel is squandered on a sea journey bound for a harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital of Libya and a Mediterranean seaport; there is another in Lebanon.

clue.text: One stopping athlete becoming more fluid

indicators.note: a piece that stops a word plugs a gap in it, so goes inside

parts.note: a runner is a track athlete
I, the Roman numeral, means one

explanation.surface: Someone halts a sprinter, who turns into something more liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: Runny means flowing or liquid, so runnier is the comparative, more fluid.

clue.text: Pressure acceptable when gripping learner beginning to acquire dance

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: one word grips another by holding it inside

parts.note: OK means acceptable
L is the learner driver's plate

indicators.note: the beginning of the word acquire is its first letter

explanation.surface: A trainee dancer, under pressure but doing fine, starts to pick up the steps.
explanation.definitionFit: The polka is a lively Bohemian couple dance in two-four time.

clue.text: Blue bonnet for US baby has not got there yet

definitions.text: baby has not got there yet

parts.note: blue films are adult films, so blue means adult
the British car bonnet is called the hood in America

explanation.surface: An American infant in a blue bonnet has not yet arrived.
explanation.walkthrough: A car's bonnet is the hinged cover over the engine; Americans call it the hood.
explanation.definitionFit: Grown-up status is the stage of life a baby has yet to reach.

clue.text: Line of South American people once enraged

parts.note: Incan describes the Incas, the old ruling people of Peru
descent is lineage, a family line

explanation.surface: A lineage from an ancient Andean people.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a charade with the pieces given in reverse order: 'Line of' the people, so the people's word comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Incandescent, literally glowing with heat, is used figuratively for furious.

clue.text: Relative bearing granddad with resistance to continue

indicators.note: a word bearing others carries them inside it

parts.note: a son is a relative
an oldie is an old person such as a granddad
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: A family member carrying grandpa, with some opposition, keeps going.
explanation.definitionFit: To soldier on is to persevere doggedly in spite of difficulty.

clue.text: Half of bees swarmed? Well judged

indicators.note: half of the four-letter word bees is two letters, here its last two

parts.note: teemed means swarmed or was crowded

explanation.surface: Did half the hive swarm? Good call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well judged' looks like a verdict on the question, but it is the definition: highly regarded.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteemed means highly regarded, rated well by others' judgment.

clue.text: Very fast making a witticism

definitions.meaning: a ... pace is a very fast one
to crack a joke is to make a witty remark

explanation.surface: A comedian rattles off quips at speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cracking is an informal word for rapid, and cracking a joke means telling one.

clue.text: Clamp left in odd place in ship

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the word for odd

parts.note: strange means odd
the hold is the cargo space in a ship

explanation.surface: A clamp was left in some peculiar spot aboard a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A stranglehold is a tight grip that clamps something, literally or in control.

clue.text: Father about to enter church for shade

indicators.note: the turned word enters, so goes inside, the church letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for father is read backwards

parts.note: a sire is a father

explanation.surface: A priest prepares to go into church to find some shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerise is a shade of bright cherry red.

clue.text: Man on board second-rate ship uneasy with old interior

parts.note: B is a second-rate grade

indicators.note: the letter for old goes in the interior of the scrambled word
uneasy suggests unsettled, so the letters of ship are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor aboard a poor vessel feels queasy, with something ancient inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man on board' suggests a sailor, but it means a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is one of the chessmen, a man on the chessboard.

clue.text: A bit daft carrying around US money in Morecambe, perhaps

indicators.note: the pieces go in the first name of the comedian

parts.note: Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian, so his first name is meant
C, for circa, means around
a cent is a coin of US money

explanation.surface: Someone slightly mad goes about with dollars in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is a seaside resort in Lancashire, but here it is Eric Morecambe, half of the comedy double act Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccentric means odd or unconventional, a little daft.

clue.text: Determined to write up records

indicators.note: in a down clue writing something up reverses it, so the phrase is read from the bottom

parts.note: set on means determined to

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to write up the minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes are written records or jottings of something.

clue.text: Tribe from Nice nice? Not totally

indicators.note: the letters come from the words without taking them in full

explanation.surface: A query about whether a tribe from the French Riviera is pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient British tribe of East Anglia led by Boudicca.

clue.text: Rock emits no water

indicators.note: to rock is to shake, so the letters of emits no are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stone gives off no water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock' and 'water' read as nouns; 'Rock' is a verb signalling the anagram and 'water' a verb defining the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To water something is to wet it or dampen it.

clue.text: Turn back on one's husband being ghastly

indicators.note: back means the word for a turn is read in reverse

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in 'your go'
re means on or concerning
one is I, so one's is I plus S

explanation.surface: Turning away from your spouse is a terrible thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ogreish means monstrous and frightful, like an ogre, so horribly unpleasant.

clue.text: Heard long joke's synopsis

indicators.note: heard says the words are spoken aloud

parts.note: to long is to die for something, and a joke is a jest, so the two words sound together

explanation.surface: Someone listens to a summary of a lengthy gag.
explanation.definitionFit: A digest is a condensed summary of written material.

clue.text: Sort inside leak that's superficial

indicators.note: the word for sort goes inside the word for leak

parts.note: to seep is to leak slowly
a kind is a sort or type

explanation.surface: A shallow sort of leak gets inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Skin-deep describes something that goes no deeper than the surface, so shallow.
